defect.evidence_quote: we decline to adopt a rule that it is always reasonable for an officer to review the entirety of the digital data seized pursuant to a warrant on the basis of the mere possibility
defect.problem: The holding is supportable, but the stored holding text is truncated after "mere…", leaving the limiting basis incomplete.
defect.proposed_fix: Complete the holding: decline a per se rule that officers may always review all seized digital data merely because evidence might conceivably be found anywhere or hidden/mislabeled/manipulated.

reasons: The opinion expressly rejects an always-reasonable, whole-device review rule for digital data seized under a warrant.
The opinion holds digital cell-phone searches must be reasonably directed to evidence of the criminal activity alleged in the warrant.
residual_risks: The page also contains a pin-36 quote, but group_inventory did not include a separate quote-fidelity or pincite row.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace the ellipsis with the full limiting phrase from the opinion.

defect.evidence_quote: The exception is not implicated in this case because “an essential predicate of the plain view doctrine is that the initial intrusion not violate the Fourth Amendment”
defect.problem: Placement under Plain View Doctrine is supported, but the role label "Key — Progeny / Refinement" overstates what the disclosed evidence shows. The opinion discusses plain view mainly to say the exception is unavailable because the search exceeded the warrant.
defect.proposed_fix: Use a softer role such as "Related — Digital warrant-scope limitation" or "Application — plain-view prerequisite" rather than "Key".

reasons: The opinion contains a plain-view analysis and cites the lawful-initial-intrusion prerequisite.
The central holding is warrant scope for digital cell-phone data, not a freestanding major refinement of plain-view doctrine.
residual_risks: No disclosed page for Plain View Doctrine supplies its inclusion criteria.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the home placement, but remove or downgrade "Key" unless the doctrine page separately treats Hughes as a leading case.
